whatIs: Ecommerce SEO is the practice of making an online store's collection, product and content pages rank in Google and appear in AI-generated answers, so the store earns traffic and orders without paying per click. It differs from general SEO because stores have hundreds of similar pages, faceted filters, variants and out-of-stock products, all of which create duplicate and thin pages that must be managed deliberately.

gaa-tha maps buying keywords to collections first — because a collection page for cold-pressed groundnut oil converts better than a blog about it — then fixes the technical layer, adds schema so Google and AI assistants can read price, availability and ratings, and builds blog clusters that link into those collections. Rankings are reported alongside organic revenue, not just positions.

faq.q: What is ecommerce SEO and how is it different from regular SEO?
faq.a: Ecommerce SEO makes a store's collection and product pages rank and get cited, and it must handle problems ordinary websites do not have: hundreds of similar pages, filter URLs, variants, seasonal stock and product schema. Regular SEO focuses on a smaller set of service or content pages. gaa-tha runs ecommerce SEO for Shopify and WooCommerce stores as a monthly retainer.

faq.q: How long does ecommerce SEO take to show results?
faq.a: Technical fixes and schema can change how pages appear within weeks, while new rankings for competitive collection keywords usually take three to six months to build. Stores with existing authority and a clean structure move faster; new domains take longer and benefit from running ads in the meantime.

faq.q: Should I optimise collection pages or write blogs?
faq.a: Collections first. A collection page that ranks for a buying keyword sends visitors straight to products, while a blog post ranks for research keywords and needs a second step. Blogs come after, in clusters that link into the collections and give AI assistants a reason to cite you.

faq.q: What schema markup does an online store need?
faq.a: Product and Offer schema with price, currency and availability, AggregateRating and Review where you have reviews, BreadcrumbList on every page and Organization on the site. Shopify themes add some by default but it is often incomplete or duplicated, so we validate every template in Search Console.

faq.q: How do you handle out-of-stock and discontinued products?
faq.a: Temporarily out-of-stock products stay live with availability schema and a back-in-stock option, because deleting them loses rankings. Discontinued products are redirected to the closest replacement or the parent collection, never left as 404 pages.

faq.q: Can ecommerce SEO get my products into ChatGPT and AI Overviews?
faq.a: It helps. AI assistants draw on pages that answer clearly, carry structured data and are cited elsewhere, so answer-first collection copy, complete schema, FAQs on product pages and consistent brand facts across the web all raise the chance of being recommended. We track AI citations as part of monthly reporting.

faq.q: Do you also run Google Shopping ads?
faq.a: Yes, through our D2C performance marketing service. The same Merchant Center feed powers free listings and paid Shopping ads, so fixing the feed for SEO improves both.
